Biswamoyopterus.distinguishing_notes: Biswamoyopterus (HB 405-540 mm) vs Petaurista (the main confusion; Sanamxay et al. 2013): yellow not orange-red incisors, bulla septae in a complex honeycomb (Petaurista <=4 septae), ears nearly naked with ear-base tufts, cheek teeth simplified and cuspidate. vs Eupetaurus: brachyodont vs hypsodont teeth, ear-base tufts present, naked-padded feet. vs Aeretes, Trogopterus, Belomys, Priapomys, Pteromys, Eoglaucomys: much larger (none exceeds 365 mm HB in the sources), cylindrical tail.

Petaurista.distinguishing_notes: Petaurista (HB 270-610 mm). vs Aeretes: narrow, normally ungrooved incisors (faint grooves in a few specimens), well-developed interfemoral membrane, mostly cylindrical tail (Allen 1940; Ellerman 1940; Li et al. 2021 key 6). vs Eupetaurus: brachyodont / at most "semi-hypsodont" teeth, orange-red incisors, no woolly fur. vs Biswamoyopterus: orange-red (not yellow) incisors and <=4 bulla septae (Sanamxay et al. 2013). vs Trogopterus: P4 not hugely enlarged, bulla septae simple; size overlaps at 270-330 mm. vs Belomys, Priapomys, Pteromys: larger (those <=250 mm). vs Eoglaucomys: posterior flexus distinct; sizes overlap at 270-305 mm. External pattern characters (white dorsal spots in P. elegans/marica, dorsal stripe in P. albiventer magnificus/P. nobilis) vary within the genus.

caveats:
QUOTES: all evidence quotes were machine-checked as substrings (after whitespace normalisation) of the retrieved source texts; OCR errors in Ellerman 1940, Allen 1940 (Internet Archive djvu text) and in Plazi renderings of HMW 2016 (e.g. "offlying", "upperincisors", "189-214-5" meaning 189-214.5) are preserved verbatim. Li et al. 2021 Table S6 rows are whitespace-normalised table rows from pdftotext.
EAR TUFTS: the brief defines ear_tufts as tufts projecting from the ear TIPS. In this group the only tufts are at the ear BASE (Trogopterus, Belomys, Biswamoyopterus, some Petaurista). For those genera ear_tufts is left "unknown" (observer ambiguity) and the sourced information is in extra character ear_base_tufts, which is the useful separator (Li et al. 2021 Table S6; Allen 1940 key).
HYPSODONTY: coded yes only for Eupetaurus. Ellerman 1940 calls Petaurista and Trogopterus teeth "semi-hypsodont"; they are coded "no" relative to the Eupetaurus condition (Ellerman's own key: "not strongly hypsodont"); phrase the key question as strongly hypsodont/Eupetaurus-like, or treat those two as unknown.
INCISOR GROOVES: "smooth" for Belomys, Eoglaucomys, Glaucomys, Pteromys (and partly Trogopterus) is an inference from HMW 2016's statement that grooved upper incisors distinguish Aeretes from all other flying-squirrel genera. Petaurista is coded smooth+grooved because faint grooves are documented in some specimens (Howell 1927 via Allen 1940; Ellerman 1940). Biswamoyopterus laoensis has "a deep groove on the inner margin" of the upper incisors, so Biswamoyopterus is unknown.
SIZE: Petaurista nujiangensis (Li et al. 2025) measurements were not retrievable (paywalled) - its HB is not verifiably within 270-610 mm. Glaucomys oregonensis is covered only via HMW 2016 G. sabrinus sensu lato. Several Biswamoyopterus/Eupetaurus/Priapomys species are known from 1-5 measured specimens, so true ranges are likely wider than reported. Belomys max 250 mm is Allen's conversion of Anderson's "about 8 inches" (likely ~203 mm) kept as a conservative bound. Sterndale 1884 gives 19.25 inches HB for "Pteromys melanopterus" from Tibet, inconsistent with all Aeretes measurements; not used.
TAXONOMY: HMW 2016 species accounts were mapped to MDD v2.5 names using Li et al. 2025 (magnificus -> P. albiventer; yunanensis, mishmiensis, mechukaensis -> P. nobilis; sybilla -> P. marica); P. grandis and P. marica have no separate HMW accounts.
NOT FOUND: no source explicitly addressing cheek pouches, tail annulation, or flank stripes for any genus in this group; these are "unknown" throughout. The patagium (present in all ten genera) separates every genus here from all co-occurring non-gliding genera, so these pattern characters are not needed within this group. Several patagium-margin colour bands could be mis-scored as flank stripes by an observer - another reason they are left unknown.
Thomas 1908 (Ann. Mag. Nat. Hist. ser. 8 vol. 1, genus diagnoses of Belomys/Trogopterus/Glaucomys) and Saha 1981 could not be retrieved (BHL blocked; Plazi stub only), and Mammalian Species accounts for Glaucomys were paywalled (403).
